long_biography.plain_text:
From Davenport, Washington, Schultz earned an electrical-engineering degree from Washington State University in 1963. He began in digital electronics and microprocessor work before helping establish Stratacom, where he combined engineering leadership with packet-network development. The company built wide-area switching systems that carried voice, data and video over digital infrastructure.

Cisco acquired Stratacom in 1996, but Schultz continued founding technology businesses. Vina Technologies developed multiservice broadband-access equipment, while Seaport Imaging made image-processing hardware and software. In retirement, he and his wife, Cindy, mentored engineering and entrepreneurship students, opening their Silicon Valley home and professional network to successive Washington State cohorts.

From Davenport, Washington, Schultz earned an electrical-engineering degree from Washington State University in 1963. He began in digital electronics and microprocessor work before helping establish Stratacom, where he combined engineering leadership with packet-network development. The company built wide-area switching systems that carried voice, data and video over digital infrastructure.

Cisco acquired Stratacom in 1996, but Schultz continued founding technology businesses. Vina Technologies developed multiservice broadband-access equipment, while Seaport Imaging made image-processing hardware and software. In retirement, he and his wife, Cindy, mentored engineering and entrepreneurship students, opening their Silicon Valley home and professional network to successive Washington State cohorts.
